subject: Reactive Variables that are modifiable by more than one action

messages.author: ab74ce81f1675322
messages.subject: Reactive Variables that are modifiable by more than one action
parts:
I'm building an app with multiple tabs that each use reactive variables to function correctly. I want to give the user lots of freedom to modify these reactive variables and am wondering about the ramifications of having a reactive variable that can be updated by more than one distinct action. 
The reactive variables I'd like to modify from more than one widget are:
- a data frame that are used for all the graphs and tables produced and can be subset by the User via widgets
- a list of samples; by default these samples will be taken from the reactive data frame above but ideally Users will be able to modify the list without automatically modifying the data frame
- an individual sample selection

Each tab of the app will be controlled by its own module that takes reactive variables in as input and returns the same reactive variables as output. My concern is that if, for example, Tab A and Tab B both offer the User the ability to modify the list of samples by clicking points on a scatter plot, moving between tabs will cause the reactive variable to be updated in unexpected ways. My expectation is that as long as the same reactive variables are fed into each module as input and returned as output, then the current value of those variables will always be defined by the User's most recent action - is this accurate? Are there any known pitfalls I'm setting myself up for with this approach?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Reactive Variables that are modifiable by more than one action
parts:
There aren't issues with reactivity per se but you may have issues with usability. For example, will clicking points on a scatter plot update the scatter plot to reflect the points you added? And if so, will it be confusing if the list/dataframe/matrix that gets updated, contains some values that aren't reflected in the scatter plot (because they were added in some other tab)?

I would caution you though to only take this approach for values that are more or less directly caused by user input. If you have other values that are *derived from* values that are directly caused by user input, then definitely use reactive expressions, not reactive values, for those if possible.
